item.title: 'It's still unclear whether Netanyahu will pay for what happened during his time in office'
item.description: As Israel marks the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, questions linger about the warnings Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received about them. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Ayala Panievsky, Lecturer at City University of London and author of The New Censorship, explains that the allegations in the run-up to the elections "are very damaging for Netanyahu but there are some factors mitigating the risk for him", including a fragmented opposition as well as the control of major media. Fuente: France 24 - English.

La plataforma de peticiones abierta por el Ministerio de Educación suma más de 40.000 recomendaciones. item.description: Maricarmen ​Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked housing ​protests in Spain, has died, Madrid's tenants' union said on Wednesday. item.title: Tasa hipotecaria a 30 años en Estados Unidos toca máximos de tres años
item.description: La tasa del préstamo hipotecario más común en Estados Unidos saltó al 7,49% anual, según la Asociación de Banqueros Hipotecarios, su nivel más alto desde noviembre de 2023 y más del doble de los que pagaban en intereses los compradores de vivienda en 2021, en plena pandemia. item.description: More than 300 people signed up for Hong Kong’s Election Committee poll as the nomination period opened on Wednesday, vying for seats on the body that chooses the city’s leader. item.title: France suspends stun grenade use at student protests
item.description: France has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at student-led demonstrations, the interior minister said Wednesday, as allegations of police brutality mounted after days of sometimes violent demonstrations across the country. Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Tuesday demanding better conditions in high schools. That same evening, President Emmanuel Macron held an emergency meeting with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and other key ministers to find a way out of the crisis. FRANCE 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from a high school in Aubervilliers, France. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
